newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank offers 3-day rrp at 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank offers 3-day rrp at 20 pct.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Friday it is offering three-day reverse repos at 20 percent.
Traders said the Central Bank was again forced to raise its rates to punish speculators and protect the peso.
The Central Bank had already lifted twice its overnight borrowing by a total of 1.75 percentage points to 13 percent on Thursday.
Despite the increases and Central Bank dollar sales, the peso had traded at a low of 26.375 early on Friday, forcing the Central Bank to move in again, traders said.
"It's costly to buy dollars now," a foreign bank dealer said.
She said, however, it may take quite a while to calm the market because of the nervousness in the region.
The peso has been hit by speculators due to the backlash from the problems of the Thai baht.
